item.text: South Australia’s Independent Commission Against Corruption studied corruption risks in public procurement to identify warning signs and improve prevention.
item.support: For these reasons the Commission has conducted a study into the corruption risks in public sector procurement.

item.text: It examined survey comments, submissions, referrals and other integrity agencies’ findings about procurement.
item.support: This report provides analysis of qualitative survey responses and submissions, reports and complaints referred to the Commission

item.text: The Commission concluded that suspected corruption was too often overlooked and that reluctance to report and poor awareness could contribute.
item.support: failure to act may also reflect a lack of awareness of behaviour that may indicate that procurement is being unduly influenced.

item.text: Its 18 recommendations covered procurement audits, training, conflicts of interest, gifts, confidential information, decision records and reporting obligations.
item.support: makes 18 recommendations to address weaknesses in public sector procurement open to exploitation

item.quote: These warning signs do not necessarily constitute corruption per se.
However, they should prompt public officers to make further enquiries and report suspicious conduct.
